/ State : Mr. Wasim Miyan, Panel Lawyer Hon'ble Shri Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice Order on Board 21/07/2023 1.

Heard Mr. Arvind Shrivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Wasim Miyan, learned Panel Lawyer, appearing for the State/respondent No.5.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he does not want to press I.A. No. 01 of 2016,
which is an application for Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18318 substituting the legal heirs of respondent No.3, who died during the pendency of this petition.

sentences.text: 3. On due consideration, I.A. No. 01 of 2016 is dismissed as not pressed.
However, learned counsel for the petitioner is directed to delete the name of respondent No.3 during the course of the date.

4. The present petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner with the following prayers :
"i) quash/set aside the order dated 04.07.2015 (Annexure P/1) passed by the learned Special/Additional Sessions Judge, District Raipur (C.G.) in Criminal Revision No. 194/14 upholding the Judicial Magistrate First Class's order dated 17.04.14 (Annexure P/2), and ii) direct the trial court to register the complaint U/s 420 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code against the respondent no. 1 to 4 and dispose off the matter as expeditiously as possible, in accordance with law."
5.

The undisputed facts of the case are that respondent No. 1 to 4 alongwith Parmeshwari Devi W/o Ramkumar Agarwal, Santoshi Devi, Sunita Devi, Anjana Devi, Manju Devi, Prabhu Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18318 Dayal, Chayya Devi, Bharti Gupta, JaiNarayan Gupta, Vishwajeet Gupta, Bharat Kumar Gupta and Sarojni Bai Agarwal had jointely purchased Land bearing Khasra No. 139/2012 part, Rakba 1.780 Hectare, Khasra No. 138/2, Rakba 0.809 hectare, Total Khasra 2, Total Rakba 2.589 hectare.

Total 6.40 Acre, located at Village Jora, Patwari Halka No. 112, Revenue Raipur,
Tahsil and District Raipur (C.G.) from the lawful possession of Bhumiswamis namely Rajkumar,
Savitri Bai, Keshar Bai, Chanda Bai, Parmeshwar, Shayama Bai, Govind, Arun, Radha Bai, Ramkali,
Pannalal and Ramsagar Bai, all R/o Village Jora, Raipur (C.G.) vide Registered sale deed dated 27.09.96.
The respondent No. 1 to 4 thus alongwith other individuals had purchased a total land of 6.40 acres, in which they in calculation had a total ownership of 1/4th of the property that is 1.60 acres.
That no partition deed was executed between them.
6. The petitioner has previous acquaintance with Ramkumar Agarwal.

The petitioner upon reference of Ramkumar Agarwal had purchased the property under the Bhumiswami rights of the Respondent Nos.1 to 4 vide Sale deed dated 17.11.98 upon monetary consideration of Rs. 5,76,000/- duly executed before witnesses.
As the partition was yet to take place, thus the respondents promised that the registry of the relevant land Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18318 i.e. 1.60 acres will be done soon after the partition.

The petitioner in the month of July 2011, came to know that the respondent No. 1 to 4, upon monetary consideration of Rs. 2,37,000/-, have releinqushed their 1/4th share of relevant land to Smt. Bharti Gupta, Shri Jai Narayan Gupta, Shri Vishwa Jeet Gupta and Bharat Gupta vide deed dated 15.03.99.

The petitioner after knowledge confided the situation with his relative Sandip Jain R/o Jungarh who asked him to come and confront the respondents in person,
which due to unavoidable business circumstances could happen only in the month of October 2011.
Upon contact

, the respondents revealed that RamKumar Agarwal upon pretext of the petitioner has fraudulently caused the registry in his name and that they instead of declaration would they would reveal it in reply if a legal notice is served to them and would also say that the amount of Rs.
2,37,000/- was also not received by them.
That upon agreement with the respondents the Petitioner duly sent them a legal notice dated 30.12.11, which was served upon them between 06.01.12 to 09.01.12.

But the respondents contrary to their promise kept on delaying the reply and later never Vijay Kumar Agrawal vs Abhiram Sahu And Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7708747/

sentences.text: fulfilled it.

7. When the petitioner again went to the respondents on 20.03.12, they straightaway refused to give anything in writing Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18318 and finally after common consensus teased the petitioner to pursue legal remedies.

The Petitioner/ Complainant, having gathered Respondent 1 to 4's ill intentions filed a complaint dated 25.04.13, before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur, C.G., alleging offences U/s 420 R/w 34.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur, C.G.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In compliance of the order of the trial court the Station Incharge submitted a positive Investigations report dated 12.08.13 before the Learned JMFC, Raipur.
The Learned Trial Court vide order dated 17.04.14 has come to a conclusion that the allegations are not made out and has dismissed the complaint.
The petitioner aggrieved by the same preferred a revision petition, which has also been dismissed by the Learned Special/Additional Sessions Judge vide order dated 04.07.15.
Hence, the present petition.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the order of the Revisional court maintaining the order of the JMFC is baseless, irrational and unwarranted and deserves to be quashed/set aside.

He further submits that the learned revisional court has erred in not appreciating the fact that the accused has not denied the agreement dated 17.11.98 executed between them and the Petitioner and on the other hand has also not negated the Relinquishment deed dated 15.03.99.
Thus the conduct was sufficient enough to have brought the ingredients of Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18318 Section 420 R/w 34 of IPC home.

Learned revisional court has also erred in realizing the fact that the Respondents in their statements recorded before the Police authorities have admitted the agreement and acceptance of the consideration and have also implicated RamKumar Agarwal.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer made by leaned counsel for the petitioner and submits that the matter relates to civil dispute which cannot be adjudged and adjudicated while exercising powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
Hence, the instant petition is liable to be dismissed.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.

11. It is trite law that at the stage of quashing, only the material of the prosecution has to be seen and the Court cannot delve into the defence of the accused and then proceed to examine the matter on its merit by weighing the evidence so produced.

The disputed questions of facts in the case cannot be adjudged and adjudicated at this stage while exercising powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and only the prima facie prosecution case has to be looked into as it is.
Evidence needs to be led to substantiate the defense of the accused.
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18318 12.

Considering the prayers and pleadings made in the instant petition and also considering the fact the matter is purely a civil dispute which cannot be looked into while exercising powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C., I do not find any ground to quash impugned order.

13. Accordingly, the instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
Vijay Kumar Agrawal vs Abhiram Sahu And Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7708747/
3 is dismissed.
